chapter: Massey Hall, race and the record business
title: Duke's royalties at Columbia, and the Tizol scene
summary: Ellington's complaint about Columbia royalties; Mingus's few meetings with him and the Tizol scene in his book.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: It is. Columbia, too. I know Duke Ellington told me that he'd signed with Columbia, how sorry he was, because his royalty checks -- his old royalty checks with RCA Victor were bigger than the ones from Columbia, for
It's sad. We're robbing our great artists. Were you -- did you see much of Duke on a friendship level?
No, I didn't go see him. There's only a few times we met. He'd always throw (Inaudible) a couple of words my way.

Well, your description of that scene with Juan Tizol in your book is one of the most beautiful and funny things I've ever read in my life. Sounds exactly like Duke. Incredible -- did you just remember that vividly?
I can see him do that, see him say that.
